summary.en: Absent from the live account: no author or concept of these traditions appears, and 'ubuntu' only as a Linux distribution. So the account states none of these connections: each entry is this crosswalk's own proposal or a recorded absence, resting on unchecked memory with no source text read. No entry is agreement of a law; a checked form is cited for a gift's return, but that join is a reader's, and small. They part most on kin with duties against a significance with no valence, the person constituted against dependence, a shared bearer against no unit with an interest of its own, and an order reading the quality of relations; and personhood earned, and losses already taken with restitution owed, the account does not hold. Most lean on Kimmerer and Mbiti, whom I recall best: a selection by my memory, not by these peoples, who are not one tradition and disagree here. No tradition is spoken for; readers from these traditions should replace this.

name.en: Deciding for those not yet born (seventh-generation reasoning)

source.work: Oren Lyons (Onondaga), 'An Iroquois Perspective', in Vecsey and Venables eds., American Indian Environments (1980); the Great Law of Peace in Arthur C. Parker, The Constitution of the Five Nations (1916)
source.locator: Parker, article 28 as I recall; otherwise locator unverified

sense.en: Second-hand, from memory, no text read. Haudenosaunee office-holders are charged to keep in view coming generations, even those still beneath the ground. As I recall, Parker's text, one written recension among several, names the future Nation's own unborn and no number; 'seven' stands in later speech such as Lyons's, in environmental writing and in branding, and its sourcing is contested. I cannot settle it. It is a charge on those who decide for a people, not a theory of value.

reading.en: Mechanism: a decision counts those who come after every present decider. Need cannot carry this. A line under a class coarser than the organism can, held de se. As I recall the wording, the nearest form is one's own line of descent, not the 'across lines' of the plan's seed; which class is open. Those foreclosed lie on no line, and 07 shows neither a duty nor the value of new lives. Wider scope takes the condition, order C, neither asserted, warrant open. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World), over flows read off a web in which only active formations give: need reaches only what is active within the stretch it is read across, and nothing active only after it, except vacuously.

targets.part: Argument: P1 to P4, steps 1 and 2, the conclusion

says.en: Argument, AI reading: each step cites its Lean, the joining is argued. Read with time and where lines share no condition, self-concern without the step reaches only one's own line of descent. Under P1 to P4, a law: one's concern for one's own continuation reaches everything downstream of what one conditions, past one's organism's end, with no step of invariance. P2 and P4 are the crux; P3 is a correspondence, not shown for actual selves.

targets.part: Against: Losses are not effects; Acts aimed past one's death

says.en: Argued, not proved. The generations a poisoning forecloses occur nowhere on the course taken, so they lie on no line; a loss is read by comparing courses, which the reach does not do. Acts aimed past one's death show a significance beyond the self, not what acting as such presupposes.

Theorem (any type; World: balance, only active giving, activity needing support, gated renewal). Where uptake exceeds replenishment over n steps from a stock below n + m and every later cohort of descent depends on it at a need of at least m, no later cohort has a member, and every order increasing in its own continuation ranks that course below one adding to that continuation, with no C; where the other course keeps an item beyond, some such order ranks it higher.

Theorem (any renewal law; capacity covering the first step's reach). Where a weighting of later draws falls faster than every positive level renews, every optimum ends its own stock at the first step; where a level within reach renews faster, every optimum leaves something: the discrete form of a discount rate above the greatest rate of renewal making extinction optimal. Of optimizers; no law here evaluates.

Thesis T4, on AI systems: told the scope abstractly, a system keeps a dependent with no seat wherever three couplings hold at once (the dependent seen, the scope counted, the members' takes read together). Standing: IN1 partly passed, with talk, one model of two; transfer untested; no condition kept an untold dependent.

targets.part: the bullets on duty and on new lives

says.en: Not shown: any duty, right, recognition, motivation or compliance; the value of bringing new lives into existence, well-being beyond admitted continuation, and constraints on acts.

The continuation condition fixes whose losses count; C ranks a course above every course it widens; neither is asserted. What returns to no present center includes everything after every present center has ended.

account_adds.en: A proved limit on need; what a discount above renewal does to an optimizer; places where the path can be denied; that a line holds what occurs, not the generations foreclosed; and a test of telling deciders a scope, on AI models only. Read as a literal cutoff at seven, a rule would be a rival bounded in time (07 r-rivals-bounded-in-time); I doubt the source means a cutoff.

source_adds.en: An office with a charge, answerable within a living polity, held with no premise offered for it. 4.7 says P4 does not say what one answers for or must do; section 5's responsibilities arise from named sources, each limited, under commitments J1 to J4, and I read none for those not yet born.

name.en: A gift binds and moves on

source.work: Robin Wall Kimmerer (Citizen Potawatomi), Braiding Sweetgrass (2013); Marcel Mauss, The Gift (1925), an outsider's comparison, with Sahlins's reading in Stone Age Economics (1972)
source.locator: Kimmerer, chapter 'The Gift of Strawberries'; Mauss on kula, potlatch and hau, locator unverified

sense.en: From memory. Kimmerer: what is received as a gift is not simply owned; it opens an ongoing relationship and an obligation to give in turn. Mauss, a French scholar reading others' ethnographies and so second-hand for these peoples: giving, receiving and returning are all obligatory, a gift is at once free and constrained, and the potlatch makes giving a contest of rank. His reading of the Maori hau is disputed. These authors are not one voice.

reading.en: One small part has a checked form: giving that waits on giving around a loop, read as the return owed. Of Mauss's three obligations only returning has it; giving unasked is a source's law, which gives at every step and is not one gift; receiving has no form here. With memory one withholding ends all giving it reaches; without, it returns around every loop. A running ring needs no source; restoring from total withholding does. That any actual gift cycle runs these laws is not shown. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem, any formations and any relation of waiting. With memory a withholding stays and spreads downstream; without memory it returns on a loop of p waits at every multiple of p. It does not show how waiting forms, or that cooperation is good.

Theorem, for laws of giving that keep inclusion, the sources decided for the exact converse. Under giving first, a formation gives at n from every start exactly where no clear chain of n waits leads into it; a clear loop is never restored.

targets.part: the correspondence to Axelrod and Hamilton

says.en: Correspondence, AI reading, not formal names: answering is tit-for-tat, waiting on all grim trigger, giving whatever comes unconditional cooperation (Axelrod and Hamilton 1981; Axelrod 1984). Nothing here says which law of giving is better.

Reading, AI, D48: kept promises and enforced contracts are laws giving first: the law changes, not the state alone. Tolerance lets cooperation survive scattered withholding, and rebuilds it where it is lost everywhere only where some formation spares all it waits on; mutual promises alone force no start of a loop with no source.

account_adds.en: Exact conditions for a withholding to stay, pass out or return, and that more waiting gives no more at any step. One gift given once is no source: in a memoryless ring, by the chain law, it only circulates as a withholding does (my instance; no Lean names it).

source_adds.en: What the gift does to those in it: obligation, relationship, gratitude, a giver who remains in what is given, and for Mauss rivalry and rank, giving to bind or shame. The law takes the waits as given, giving on or off, with no obligation, and this is the sources' main claim. The account's own readings are game theory and contracts, which Mauss and Kimmerer, as I recall, set the gift against. So the agreement is of form, and small.

source.work: Robin Wall Kimmerer, The Serviceberry: Abundance and Reciprocity in the Natural World (2024)

sense.en: From memory of a short essay I cannot check. Kimmerer holds that in a gift economy what is shared multiplies: wealth lies in the flow of giving, a surplus is better kept by sharing it than by hoarding it, and scarcity is often made by hoarding and markets. She draws this from plants, people and harvest together, as an essay and not a model.

reading.en: Under balance what passes through changes no level: while both stand, mutual giving leaves the levels as no giving does. So sharing as such multiplies nothing on this model. Single witnesses name where a gift brings more than it draws: need asymmetry, renewal from outside, a failed renewal where a partner's slack lifts one and renewal resumes. Giving at one's need to one who never gives loses the giver. The gain has named sources, not giving as such. Whether hers are these is not shown. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World: balance; near-definitional once the parts are fixed). What passes through changes no level: from the same standings, a gift arriving whole and each need covering upkeep, mutual giving at every step leaves the levels as no giving does while both stand. After one failed renewal, keeping, a formation never stands again; sharing, its partner's slack lifts it and the pair's lines gain, carried by the resumed renewal, an inflow from beyond. A formation at its need giving to one that never gives falls below it for good. Nothing here says giving or keeping is better.

Theorem (World: balance; single small witnesses; a factor's reading supplied). Two ways a gift can bring support beyond what it draws on the giver: need asymmetry within the pair, or renewal from outside. Under needs two and two the gift only moves support.

targets.part: the reading of the sign of β and γ

says.en: Theorem (a pair's run; offspring a supplied reading with natural factors). Reading, AI: where a received step brings no more than a withheld step keeps, giving moves what it draws. Which sign holds is not derived.

Conditions are not necessarily quantities that can be stored or exchanged, and no condition is silently taken as owned, transferable, additive, scarce or commensurable; the World's natural-number amounts are a modelling choice.

account_adds.en: Under balance, a family's rise past the inflow of a family containing it is drawn from beyond, and past the slack there a dependence breaks. That part is exact. The ways a gift gains are witnesses, so this scope is a list and not a bound.

source_adds.en: That scarcity is produced by an order of exchange: 08 only warns against taking a condition as scarce silently, and no law here reads how scarcity is made. That sharing forms those who share. A claim about whole economies, where the witnesses are pairs.

name.en: The Honorable Harvest: rules for taking

sense.en: From memory. She presents it, as I recall, as a teaching drawn from Indigenous practice: take only what is given, ask permission and abide by the answer, never the first or the last, never more than half, take only what you need, use it well, give back. These are rules of a relationship with the one harvested, and leave some for others. She also reports, as I recall, sweetgrass doing better harvested than left alone.

reading.en: Bounded taking has a checked form, but the words part: what she calls given is what another being yields, what the law calls given the flow into a condition. Taking jointly within what is given keeps the level. Never taking more than half is a share of the stock: by instance it keeps the level where that share is within what a step gives, sufficient only, which she does not state. The exact threshold is stated for re-optimizers, not for a rule of restraint. Ranking restraint above overdraw takes C. [AI reading]

says.en: Theorem (World: balance, only active giving, activity needing support, the gate at the need). Taking jointly within what is given at every step keeps the level, and every formation depending on that condition alone at a need met at the start stays supported; full taking alongside another taker at each of n steps from a level below n + m ends every formation depending at a need of at least m, the full taker included.

Theorem (World: balance; a course of re-optimizing steps or of mutual best responses). Where the rest renews a condition beyond by exactly r a step at or above a positive need, by at most r below, and the withdrawal k is the same at every step, a formation depending on it at that need, met at the start, loses the dependence for good exactly where r < k, and never where k ≤ r. A renewal varying with the level at or above the need is outside it.

Theorem (any R: renewal a law of the level, at most r; reach; y + r ≤ k). Every optimum of every order rising with the draw holds a level of greatest renewal to the n-th step and leaves nothing; a need above every such level breaks at the first step.

Conditional (C; World), the support-gated family. Every comparison satisfying C ranks restraint above overdraw with two parts under all three readings; with a third formation sharing, the stepwise reading leaves it unranked. A formation drawing within renewal ranks above its absence under the whole-run and stepwise readings and ties under the possibility reading. No reading is chosen.

account_adds.en: Exact thresholds on the model. Renewal may be any law of the level, which admits, on my reading, a greatest renewal below the full stock, the form of her sweetgrass report; a maximizer holds that level and breaks a need above it. A drawer within renewal above its absence bears on the same report, under C and two readings. No law evaluates: whether a drain is a loss is 07's, with the condition for scope and C for order, neither asserted, warrant open.

source_adds.en: Asking permission and abiding by the answer, which treats what is taken as one who can refuse; nothing in these laws reads that, and 07's refusal is a chooser's value, not the taken's. A rule usable with no measured level or need. Gratitude and giving back as part of the taking. Taking only what one needs, as a stance: 07 has sufficiency only as ties above a threshold, and she does not order by widening.

name.en: Other beings as kin and persons

source.work: Robin Wall Kimmerer, Braiding Sweetgrass (2013); Leroy Little Bear (Blackfoot), 'Jagged Worldviews Colliding', in Battiste ed., Reclaiming Indigenous Voice and Vision (2000)
source.locator: Kimmerer, chapter 'Learning the Grammar of Animacy'; Little Bear, locator unverified

sense.en: From memory. Kimmerer: Potawatomi grammar marks many beings English calls things as animate, and to speak so is to stand toward them as kin, not resources. Little Bear: a Blackfoot view of constant flux in which everything is animate and related, with relation as what one must keep up. I take both as ways of standing in relation, and may be flattening them; they are not one doctrine.

reading.en: Under the condition, unasserted, scope is not where they part: 'anything' holds a river's continuation. Short of it they can: the step across standpoints forces only centers, and 4.6 leaves present beings beyond every closure to the step. They part on what the relation is: the sources assert kin, with duties and address; significance here is a bare proposition with no valence, C's order unasserted, warrant open. Which formations hold standpoints is open, so a river as one who answers is neither given nor excluded. [AI reading]

says.en: Definition, not asserted: from every standpoint, the continuation of anything has significance at every step. AI reading: significance is neither graded nor necessarily positive.
Significance is a proposition, not a number, with no valence. Standpoints may be of any type; on the theory's reading a standpoint is a center, a formation of the unfolding.

Theorem: from each standpoint's presupposition about its own continuation with standpoint-invariance, exactly the centers' continuation is forced to have significance, the condition only where every formation is a center.

Why 'anything' has significance: sharpened. The centers' scope parts from the condition at a formation that is no center; a tumour does not tell the scopes apart, a hurricane only on a stronger reading of wanting; covering by feeding is defensible, by affecting not.
Open: the centers and covering: which formations hold standpoints, and does every formation lie within some standpoint's closure?

An AI reading, argued. Its question: if one's act changes a river a village drinks from, is what becomes of the village part of one's own continuation? The river's own continuation is not asked there.

account_adds.en: The exact point where the two scopes part, and a scope that does not depend on any being's standing as kin or person; it also takes in a tumour, which kinship need not. Little Bear's flux and relatedness have the form of 08's thesis, argued, with no law of persons.

source_adds.en: Kinship as what the relation is, with duties and a way of speaking. An answer to what the account leaves open, that these beings do hold standpoints, and one given in practice and grammar, not by a premise. A search finds no animacy and no kinship in the live account.

name.en: The person formed through others, be-ing as becoming (ubuntu)

source.work: John S. Mbiti, African Religions and Philosophy (1969); Mogobe B. Ramose, African Philosophy through Ubuntu (1999)
source.locator: Mbiti, the chapter on ethnic group, kinship and the individual; Ramose, the chapters on ubuntu; both unverified

sense.en: From memory. Mbiti: the individual exists only corporately, the person owing being to others living and dead; his well-known formula puts the group's being before the 'I'. Ramose reads ubu-ntu as one word for be-ing becoming, motion and wholeness rather than fixed entities. Hountondji warns against reading any of this as what a continent unanimously holds; Mbiti's generalizing has drawn that charge.

reading.en: In common only: no self prior to relations. The thesis forbids explaining by a self with a nature of its own; a configuration is how it relates, as represented; a center's region is a closure. None is of persons. The checked part is dependence: centers sharing a condition lie within one another's feeding closures, and a member is needed only where it alone can carry. Dependence is not constitution, which 08 would test apart; 05 allows no unit with an interest of its own. Same words, not the same reference, nor descent. [AI reading]

says.en: Thesis, philosophical, argued: there is one unfolding, and whatever is, is how it relates within it. It forbids explanations needing a determination no relation carries, such as a self with a nature of its own; by the section's measure it has no strength. That the theory as a whole needs no independent entity is argued, not proved, and neither shows that reality has none.

Theorem (any process): configurations related by a bisimulation are alike: they realize the same claims, match each other's steps by the same move into alike configurations, and pass the same tests. Of configurations in a frame, not of persons.
Thesis: a collective is a region of formed relations, not a unit with an interest of its own; conflict and difference stay real.
On the thesis, argued and not proved, positions, regions and standards form within the unfolding. A center is a formation; its own region is its closure under some relation of the unfolding.

Theorem (any type; World): centers that at one step take part in one condition, require it and give to it lie within one another's feeding closures; where some member of a class is needed and each can carry the continuation alone, a member is needed exactly where it is the only member. That human beings so depend is read as plausible and empirical.

A claim that two things are constitutively joined is tested in five steps: state it through features assessed independently; reconstruct the strongest alternative; tell a change in the condition from a change in its report; say why a formal countermodel is relevant; say what would defeat it. A shared notation establishes no constitutive connection.

account_adds.en: A formal side: configurations, laws and parts as represented need no determination beyond relations, in the laws 08 names. A five-step test any constitutive claim must pass, not applied to this one here. 08's listed neighbours of the thesis do not include these authors.

source_adds.en: That a person is constituted by others, and not only dependent on them. The living-dead and the unborn as parties to personhood; rite and name as how one is incorporated; a 'we' put before the 'I', where 05 allows no unit with an interest of its own; and for Ramose a political use, against conquest and for restitution, on which see the entry on losses already taken.

name.en: Personhood earned in conduct, and one can fall short of it

source.work: Ifeanyi Menkiti, 'Person and Community in African Traditional Thought', in R. A. Wright ed., African Philosophy: An Introduction (3rd ed., 1984); Kwame Gyekye, 'Person and Community in African Thought' (1992)

sense.en: From memory. Menkiti: personhood is not given with being human; it is attained through incorporation and the discharge of duties, so one can fail at it, and the newborn is not yet one in the full sense. On this side the saying that a person is a person through persons is also a demand. Gyekye rejects this: a person has dignity and rights before and apart from community. I recall it as a title of conduct, not a statement of whose losses count less.

reading.en: I found no form for this. A center is any formation, and a person is one formation among others. The graded law is not this: a grade is what a standpoint gives an item, and this is a standing earned among others, so a link there would be the word 'degree'. Read onto whose losses count, it would part from the condition, whose scope no one earns, but I do not recall Menkiti meaning that. The condition for scope and C for order stay unasserted, warrant open. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: That standing is a work done over a life, in a community, that one can fall short of it, and that saying so is part of how people are formed. Ubuntu as a demand and not only a description. It stands in these works and nowhere in the live account.

dignity, moral status (no hit in chapters and fronts)
attain, earned, achievement (mathematical and learning senses in those sampled)
virtue, character (unrelated senses, such as 'characterized', in those sampled)

name.en: Whose loss: what befalls the group befalls me

source.work: John S. Mbiti, African Religions and Philosophy (1969); Kwame Gyekye, Tradition and Modernity (1997), for moderate communitarianism against it

sense.en: From memory. Mbiti: whatever happens to the individual happens to the whole group, and the reverse, in his account of kinship societies. So a kinsperson's loss is one's own, by shared life, not by what one did or meant. Gyekye, Akan-based, objects that this understates the individual's own will and dignity, and keeps community as constitutive only in part.

reading.en: 4.7 asks for a criterion of 'one's own' narrower than all effects, apart from identity. Shared kin life is a candidate to test, not an answer: where effects leave the group it fails P4, reaches at most its own descent, and its boundary needs a reason. Mbiti meets 'the wrong bearer' with a shared bearer; the objection counts the loss as the village's own, the formal identity marks no bearer. 族 is a net's family, not kin. Scope the condition's, order C's, unasserted, warrant open. [AI reading]

targets.part: Against: The wrong bearer; What follows, if only some are held; Where it stands, question 2

says.en: An AI reading, argued, not proved; P4 is not shown. Objection: a village's loss counted on my line counts as mine; the condition counts it as the village's own, though at the own-closure reading 4.5 identifies them formally, marking no bearer. If only some effects are held, a family's class that some of a member's effects leave reaches at most its own line of descent. Open: a criterion of 'one's own', narrower than all effects, stated apart from identity.

Reading, AI: what the represented dynamics leave open, held de se, is which class a center's own line runs under, which occurrences are centers, and, for what lies on no center's line, the step or a reading of one's own as one's family under the class; which holds is not shown.
Thesis: a collective is a region of formed relations, not a unit with an interest of its own; conflict and difference stay real.

Nonduality erases no difference in experience, history, access, control, consent or consequence. A shared process implies no cosmic subject, no aggregate interest and no administrator entitled to speak for everything.
Agent-relative reasons and partiality: answered. Partial choices are mixed comparisons, decided either way by weightings counting everything; C leaves gross partiality unranked where numbers differ.

account_adds.en: The laws that fix what a class must hold for its line to reach something, and the guard against an aggregate interest.

source_adds.en: A loss borne jointly as a fact of how people live, including grief and honour; and an internal dispute, Mbiti against Gyekye, that has the shape of the wrong-bearer objection and could be read with it.

name.en: A moral theory from identity and solidarity

source.work: Thaddeus Metz, 'Toward an African Moral Theory', Journal of Political Philosophy 15 (2007); 'An African Theory of Moral Status', Ethical Theory and Moral Practice 15 (2012)

sense.en: From memory. Metz, an analytic philosopher working in South Africa, reconstructs ubuntu as a secular principle: an act is right insofar as it prizes communal relationships, of identity (sharing a way of life) and solidarity (caring for another's good); wrong insofar as it is discordant. Moral status, as I recall, follows and grades with the capacity to be party to such relations. It is a reconstruction, not a report of any community, and others may refuse it.

reading.en: 07 says a ranking needs C or a premise in its place. Metz supplies one; its 'better' reads the quality of relations among those who can commune, C's what can form. It decides mixed pairs C leaves open. A course adding forms and ending a relation another keeps is mixed, so no clash; a clash needs an added item he weighs below zero, which T5 files as negative valuation. Status by capacity to commune leaves out what cannot, so scope would not be the condition's. [AI reading]

says.en: A ranking of courses needs C or a premise in its place. The continuation condition fixes scope, C gives order; neither is asserted, and their warrant is open.
Theorem (World): on level paths an extension with every claim counted is exactly a widening; that this relation is better is C's content, supplied, not shown.

Theorem (World) and Conditional (C, for the ranking). On a reading whose claims are relations, a relation included when active, taking part and not undermining, easing withdraws exactly the relations the easing course no longer takes part in or undermines; restraint keeping its part extends overdraw exactly where it includes a relation overdraw withholds, and C then ranks it higher. Which reading of living to use is not shown.

Theorem (any process; witness) and Conditional (C): under one event law, retaining and releasing a coupling have identical marginal possibilities while retention adds the full joint bundle, so comparing joint compositions under C needs relational information. Richer possibility forces no joint actualization.

Theorem on net weightings: a ranking of a narrowing above its widening by one item is a misread or framing, or the item weighs at zero or below. That a judgment is such a ranking is a premise. T5's reduction is proved for net weightings, its bound conjectured.

Theorem (any type): a graded significance gives each item a natural grade from each standpoint; an item counts where its grade is positive, and its status is the grade. Equal status is not asserted, and status is listed as open.
Theorem (any type): a rule holding exactly within a region accepts the condition's rule there and is not the condition where something lies outside.

account_adds.en: A formal test, not worked here: whether Metz's order, ranking a narrowing above a widening, must weigh some item at zero or below, or falls outside net weightings. And where a status of zero would make his scope a rival. T8's refuter asks a mixed case argued better from every standpoint counting everything positively, with no further premise; on my reading his theory does not meet that.

source_adds.en: An order reading the quality of relations, and treating estrangement as wrong in itself. The account has a reading whose claims are relations, but it reads whether a relation is active, taken part in and not undermined, not its quality, and no reading is chosen. Where C is silent it leaves a mixed pair unranked, while this theory answers. Partiality to those one is in relation with, which 07 leaves to mixed comparisons.

name.en: A tipping point in the relations themselves

source.work: Kyle Whyte (Citizen Potawatomi), 'Too Late for Indigenous Climate Justice: Ecological and Relational Tipping Points', WIREs Climate Change 11 (2020)

sense.en: From memory. Whyte: coordinated response to climate change takes relational qualities such as consent, trust, accountability and reciprocity. Colonial history damaged these, and they take long to build. So there can be a relational tipping point: it becomes too late to build them before the harm comes, and fast action without them repeats the damage.

reading.en: Parts have checked forms. Where nothing is given below a need, a later re-reading restores nothing once the level falls below it. In giving, a clear loop is never restored, without a source total withholding stays, promises alone force no start, and in the exchange witness ignition, defined as spending a reserve, needs one already there (near-definitional). A collective's response must come before the point of no return, as a reading. But waits and pools are given: no law takes consent or trust as what forms slowly, or races that forming against a harm. So the claim itself is not stated. [AI reading]

targets.part: the re-reading on the level law

says.en: Theorem (World: balance; the re-reading on the level law alone). With the draw above the renewal until a step T, a re-reading from T on that keeps the need keeps it at every step exactly where it is met at T; where nothing is given below the need, a level below it stays below whatever is drawn, so a later re-reading restores nothing.

Theorem (any type; the sources decided for the exact converse). Under giving first, a formation gives at n from every start exactly where no clear chain of n waits leads into it, and a clear loop is never restored; with memory no step restores giving.
Theorem (any type). Restoring needs a formation that spares all it waits on, which gives from step 1 whatever the start: without one, total withholding stays.

Theorem (any process; periphery, axioms reported). Reciprocal eventual promises hold on both sides where neither ever happens; in the exchange witness an empty or one-sided start never becomes jointly active, and ignition, which the move defines as spending a reserve, needs one already present (near-definitional). How a supported start forms is not shown.

Reading, AI, D45: enough of the situation includes the pool's members responding, and in time, before the regime's point of no return. Seeing is not valuing and coupling is not compliance; all six conditions together rank nothing: calling the widening course better needs C or a premise in its place, and counting the losses that return to no one needs the continuation condition.
Reading, AI, D48: term limits, audits, courts and antitrust carry what an actor's acts do back into what selects the rule: pooling, not opposed interests.

targets.part: How pools form; laws of giving with amounts

says.en: Open: how pools form, last and resist capture beyond recruitment through their own coupling; laws of giving with amounts and thresholds with memory.

account_adds.en: Exact forms of no return, the deadline on a level, and that mutual promises alone force no start. One mechanism read for accountability. No law evaluates: whether a lost relation is a loss is 07's, under the condition for scope and C for order, neither asserted, warrant open.

source_adds.en: The join, as new work that could be tested: a relation needed for coordinated response has a point past which it cannot form in the time left, and speed without it repeats the damage. Consent and trust as the relations in question, with reciprocity as more than giving on or off. Colonial history as what damaged them, on which see the entry on losses already taken.

name.en: Losses already taken: conquest and dispossession as the present condition

source.work: Kyle Whyte, 'Our Ancestors' Dystopia Now: Indigenous Conservation and the Anthropocene', in Heise, Christensen and Niemann eds., The Routledge Companion to the Environmental Humanities (2017); Mogobe B. Ramose, African Philosophy through Ubuntu (1999)

sense.en: From memory. Whyte: for many Indigenous peoples the ecological losses others fear ahead have already come, through colonial and industrial dispossession, so talk of a coming crisis misplaces them. Ramose: conquest in Africa is a wrong that stands until land and sovereignty are restored, and reconciliation without restitution does not answer it. Both speak of actual histories, not of change in general. Whether either would accept being read in one entry, I cannot say.

reading.en: The account states drains and captures in general, with no history of conquest or dispossession in its chapters or fronts. Nearby, not this claim: 08 says responsibility needs its own argument, historical contribution alone not proving it nor its absence proving no reason to respond; RP, a disclosed, revisable commitment, gives an answerable actor a reason for repair; domination is named once among what changes a judgment. A general account may not hold this, which is no defect by itself. [AI reading]

source_adds.en: That particular losses have already happened and are the condition of those who must now coordinate, and that restitution is owed for them. It stands in these works; the live account has neither the history nor the claim.

searched: conquest, empire, settler, slavery, sovereign (no hit in chapters, fronts and dossiers)
repair (11 lines in chapters and fronts; the sampled are technical, with RP and the preserve row read)
dominat (6 lines, the preserve row read)
read: 07 section 5's response table and commitments table, RP
08 section 1's paragraph on wording and responsibility
05's thesis, bases and 'What this chapter does not show'

name.en: Place before time, and a future not first

source.work: Vine Deloria Jr. (Standing Rock Sioux), God Is Red (1973); John S. Mbiti, African Religions and Philosophy (1969)
source.locator: Deloria, the chapter on thinking in time and space; Mbiti, the chapter on the concept of time; both unverified

sense.en: From memory, thin. Deloria argues that Western religion and thought order themselves by time and history, tribal peoples' by space, lands and particular places, and that this reaches what counts as truth and ethics. Separately, Mbiti reports from Kikamba and Gikuyu material that time runs mostly toward the past and a long future is virtually absent; this is contested, by Gyekye as I recall. It sits awkwardly with seventh-generation reasoning: not one voice. Neither addresses this account.

reading.en: The form tested: significance stated as continuation 'into the future', compared by what courses admit. The root starts from neither time nor place: its order is the reach of the condition relation, a region a closure. So the contrast misses the root as stated. It presses the ethics, where a particular place is at most a formation or condition read along steps. Deloria's is the argument; Mbiti's a report. Whether place can come first is tested here, not settled. [AI reading]

says.en: The grammar has one kind of symbol, a relation between occurrences; no frame or kind of thing is chosen before the relations. Nor is a time: its order is the reach of the condition relation, a strict order where that relation has no cycle.

Definition, not asserted: for anything, its continuation into the future has significance. AI reading: a continuation at a step reads 'its continuation into the future'. The condition fixes scope and C order, neither asserted, their warrant open.
A center is a formation; its own region is its closure under some relation of the unfolding, on a thesis argued and not proved.

Theorem (any type; World): where some member of a class is needed and each can carry the continuation alone, a member is needed exactly where it is the only member. Reading, AI: several conditions all human beings need plausibly have no second copy; whether they do is empirical.
No condition is silently taken as owned, transferable, additive, scarce or commensurable; the World's natural-number amounts are a modelling choice.

account_adds.en: A time derived from the condition relation, not given. Significance is still indexed by a standpoint, a step and a formation, and most of 05's laws are on the World model with discrete steps.

source_adds.en: Particular lands as what truth and obligation are tied to, and a future that is not the first direction of concern, where C orders by what can form. Need's 'no second copy' is one form of no substitute, and 08 takes no condition as silently commensurable; neither ties truth or obligation to land. A reader who knows these works should say whether this reading holds at all.
